subject: Gateway adapter onboarding: SDK samples, endpoint migration, and rate-safety playbook
messages:
From: Samir Das <samir@spexle.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Gateway adapter onboarding: SDK samples and cutover window

Hi Mateo + Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. We're kicking off the engineering handoff for the Gateway Adapter work (Spexle -> Redwood). High level: our infra team will point traffic at your new adapter endpoints in two phases (staging canary, then prod cutover). Before we schedule, could you share: SDK quickstart snippets (Node/Python), an endpoint migration checklist, and your recommended retry/timeouts + rate-fencing guidance for our burst-y traffic (we see 3-4x spikes during settlement windows).

What we need from Redwood:
- Minimal SDK init for client + sample calls we can drop into our adapter
- Endpoint migration checklist (DNS cutover / health checks / fallback)
- Retry matrix (idempotent vs non-idempotent calls, backoff windows)
- Guidance on token rotation and per-API rate limits (we'll likely open 8 concurrent connections per region)

Proposed canary window: Jan 20 22:00 - 23:00 UTC (staging -> 5% traffic), prod cutover Jan 21 02:00 - 04:00 UTC. Can you confirm availability and any preflight items we should complete?

Attaching our current traffic shape summary (referenced as attachment in this thread).

Thanks,
Samir Das
Senior Systems Engineer | Spexle Inc
attachments: spexle-traffic-summary.csv (attachment stub)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Samir Das <samir@spexle.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-12T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Gateway adapter onboarding: SDK samples and cutover window

Samir — thanks for the details. High-level plan below and I've attached three artifacts: redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip (samples + integration test), endpoint-migration-checklist.pdf, retry-matrix.xlsx.

Quick plan (we'll iterate during a short runbook call):
1) Preflight (we review auth, CORS, SNI, and a smoke test suite) — 48h before canary
2) Staging canary (5% traffic) — monitor p95 latency, 429s, and error budget; validate rollback path
3) Gradual ramp to prod if no regressions; final DNS cutover with 5-10 minute observation windows

SDK quick examples (from the zip, dropping here for convenience):
Node (minimal):
const { RedwoodClient } = require('redwood-sdk');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, region: 'us-west-2', timeoutMs: 60000 });
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'rw-small-1', prompt: 'Hello' });

Python (minimal):
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['RW_API_KEY'], timeout=60)
resp = client.generate(model='rw-small-1', prompt='Hello')

Endpoint migration notes (abridged):
- Health checks: /_status (200) every 10s for 3 successive successes
- Fallback: 502s should trigger immediate rollout to previous variant and increase prefetched KV cache
- DNS TTL: lower to 60s 24h before cutover

Retry & timeout guidance (summary from attached retry-matrix.xlsx):
- Idempotent calls (embeddings, GETs): 3 attempts, exponential backoff starting at 200ms, max backoff 2s
- Non-idempotent (stateful generation with streaming): prefer client-side client.request-id dedup + 1 retry only, linear backoff 500ms
- Global per-API rate fences: recommend limiting to 10 RPS per token-type across a single connection; open multiple connections for concurrency but shard keys to avoid head-of-line

Token rotation: recommend short-lived keys (1h) with a refresh endpoint. If you need HSM/KMS integration for Private, we can walk through it during the runbook.

Canary window Jan 20 22:00 UTC works for our infra team; we can cover the preflight checklist on Jan 19. I've CC'd Kimberly to coordinate the smoke tests and Vivek for rate-fencing rules.

Notes on monitoring hooks we will expose:
- /observability/trace-id in responses for request-level tracing
- per-route token-level usage metrics via the Console (we'll share a dashboard link)

Next step: confirm Jan 19 10:00 PT (17:00 UTC) preflight call?

— Mateo Alvarez
Technical CSM, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip, endpoint-migration-checklist.pdf, retry-matrix.xlsx

On Tue, Jan 12, 2026 at 11:05 AM Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:

> const { RedwoodClient } = require('redwood-sdk');
> const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, region: 'us-west-2', timeoutMs: 60000 });
>
> Endpoint migration notes (abridged): DNS TTL: lower to 60s 24h before cutover

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Quick clarifications:
- For token rotation, do you have a recommended refresh endpoint pattern or library to call from our adapter?
- On rate-fencing: the 10 RPS per token is fine but our bursts hit 30 RPS for ~60s. Is it better to open more connections or rely on client-side queuing/backpressure?

We'll join the Jan 19 preflight call. Also, can you include a very small retry helper snippet we can copy into our adapter (prefer JS + Python)? If you already have that in the zip, point me to the file name.

Thanks,
Samir

PS — contracts expect a simple SLO clause; I'm copying contracts@ so we can align on the production SLA window later.

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samir Das <samir@spexle.com>, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-15T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Gateway adapter onboarding: SDK samples and cutover window (preflight confirmed)

Samir — thanks for the signal. Confirming internal owners and preflight cadence:
- Preflight call: Jan 19 10:00 PT (17:00 UTC) — agenda: auth checks, smoke tests, alert thresholds, rollback plan
- Canary: Jan 20 22:00 - 23:00 UTC (staging -> 5%)
- Prod ramp: Jan 21 02:00 - 04:00 UTC (target full cutover post-observation)

Preflight checklist (short):
- Credentials: ephemeral API key provisioning + refresh endpoint validated
- SDK smoke tests: run sample/generate.test.js and samples/quick_smoke.py (in redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip)
- Load profile: run a 1-minute burst at 3x expected load against staging to validate retry/backoff behaviour
- Observability: shared dashboard + request-level trace-id enabled

Attached items are the canonical copies — use these in your runbook: endpoint-migration-checklist.pdf, retry-matrix.xlsx, redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip.

Kimberly — can you run the smoke tests on Jan 19 and drop the results in the Drive link? Vivek — please prepare a short note on recommended connection sharding vs queuing for bursts (Samir: our recommendation will be to shard connections + soft client-side queue, with short-term token leasing to avoid head-of-line).

Looking forward to the preflight. If anything changes on your side ping me directly.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Manager, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
attachments: endpoint-migration-checklist.pdf, retry-matrix.xlsx, redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip
